newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat lower, new lows set as SRW sales slow.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat lower, new lows set as SRW sales slow.

text.p: CBOT hard red winter wheat was lower at midsession and new lows were set on disappointment about the sales pace for soft red winter wheat, traders said.

"There was no soft red winter business and even though prices are starting to get competitive, there's still a lot of wheat around the world and overall the values are cheap," said Skip Searcy wheat trading specialist for FIMAT Futures.

Egypt over the weekend bought 100,000 tonnes of U.S. soft white wheat, Pakistan is in the market for 200,000 tonnes of white wheat and Algeria Monday announced a snap tender for 100,000 tonnes of optional-origin wheat.
Last week Algeria bought wheat from Argentina and France rather than the United States.
Traders said funds continued to add to their short positions in the wheat pit.
"The commitments showed funds were short and I think that will get bigger," Searcy said of the most recent Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitments of Traders data.
Friday's CFTC report showed non-commercials, including funds, were short nearly two to one as of October 22.
At 1135 CST, wheat was 6-1/4 cents per bushel lower to 1/2 up, with December down 6-1/4 at $3.83-1/2 a bushel.
New contract lows were set early Monday in the March and May with the new low for March as of 1140 CST at $3.77-1/2 a bushel, down from the previous low of $3.78 set Friday.

The CFTC report Friday showed as of October 22, non-commercials were short wheat 81.930 million bushels and long 42.485 million. Since October 8 the short tally increased 10.490 million bushels and longs increased 195,000 bushels.

The key moving averages showed wheat remains bearish and the nine day relative strength index as of 1145 CST was at 22 points. Technicians generally consider an RSI of 30 or less as indicative of an oversold market.
First support in the December was at $3.83-1/2 a bushel and second support was at $3.72-3/4. First resistance was at $3.93-3/4 and second resistance at $4.04-1/4.
The session low for December was $3.82-1/2 and the session high was $3.90.
